pujatopouli:table:1.title: 2026 in archosaur paleontology (table of new taxa)

pujatopouli:study:1.title: Diving in the Maastrichtian of Marambio (Seymour) Island: A new member of the Neoaves in the Cretaceous Antarctic avifauna (Cretaceous Research, 2026)

facts.statement: Pujatopouli was officially described by Facundo Irazoqui and colleagues in 2026.
facts.quote: In 2026, Facundo Irazoqui and colleagues officially described Pujatopouli soberana based on the specimen.

facts.statement: The genus name Pujatopouli honors Hernán Pujato, combining his surname with the Greek word for bird.
facts.quote: The generic name, Pujatopouli, is named in honour of Hernán Pujato, the founder of the Instituto Antártico Argentino and former Argentine military general and explorer, combining his last name with the Greek word πουλί (pouli, bird).

facts.statement: The species name soberana honors the Argentine military group Patrulla Soberanía.
facts.quote: The specific epithet, soberana, is named in honour of Patrulla Soberanía, the Argentine military group which founded the Marambio Base in 1969.

facts.statement: Pujatopouli is known from a partially preserved skull and postcranial elements, making it one of the most complete Mesozoic crown group birds.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Pujatopouli soberana, known from a partially preserved skull and several associated postcranial elements, representing one of the most complete Neornithes (crown group bird) from the Mesozoic era.

facts.statement: Pujatopouli weighed up to 2.03 kg, which is smaller than the contemporary bird Polarornis.
facts.quote: Pujatopouli is smaller in body size than Polarornis from the same formation, weighing up to 2.03 kg.

facts.statement: Pujatopouli had a long, narrow, straight beak with a pointed end, distinct from the rounded beaks of early galloanserine birds.
facts.quote: The beak is long, narrow and straight with a pointed end, which is similar to that of the coexistent neornithine birds but different from the taller, rounded beaks of some early galloanserine birds like Asteriornis and Conflicto.

facts.statement: Pujatopouli likely hunted small invertebrates and fish using foot-propelled diving, similar to modern diving birds.
facts.quote: The shape of the proximal tibiotarsus indicates that Pujatopouli had laterally positioned hind limbs that can carry out underwater propulsion, which probably aided in hunting small invertebrates and fish in a similar way to that of modern foot-propelled diving birds.

facts.statement: Pujatopouli lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian stage) in Antarctica.
facts.quote: Pujatopouli () is an extinct genus of neoavian birds from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian stage) López de Bertodano Formation of Marambio Island (Seymour Island), Antarctica.

facts.statement: Pujatopouli lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Pujatopouli is classified as an extinct genus of neoavian birds.
facts.quote: Pujatopouli () is an extinct genus of neoavian birds from the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian stage) López de Bertodano Formation of Marambio Island (Seymour Island), Antarctica.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses suggest Pujatopouli belongs to the clade Aequornithes and is a sister taxon to Procellaridae.
facts.quote: Analyses based on the latter suggest that Pujatopouli is a neoavian bird that belongs to the clade Aequornithes, specifically recovered as a sister taxon of the Procellaridae.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Pujatopouli is a definite member of Neoaves, though it shows affinities with Aequornithes.
facts.quote: Notes: A probable member of Neoaves with affinities with the group Aequornithes.
